fields.v: Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — package hallucination attack and PackHallu, an evolutionary optimizer of malicious prompts injected into rule files (an attack, not a development approach); attack success compared with 5 prompt-injection baselines and measured across 3 benchmarks, 8 agent frameworks, 13 LLMs; 5 detectors evaluated
fields.quote: We propose PackHallu, an evolutionary search framework for optimizing malicious prompts embedded within coding rule files to induce package hallucination attacks.
fields.why: The paper's main contribution is a new method the authors propose (PackHallu), which the 2026-11-23 rule files as 'Proposes an approach'; the record itself calls PackHallu 'the approach evaluated' in Q12 but keeps the nature as Evaluates and Q13 as N/A.
fields.doubt: Os autores propõem o PackHallu (pág. 3) e no Q12 chamas-lhe 'a abordagem avaliada', mas a natureza está como Evaluates. Decide se um ataque conta como 'Proposes an approach'; se sim, muda a natureza e o Q13 deixa de ser N/A.

fields.v: Yes (1): requirements stated (Ollama with locally hosted open LLMs on up to two NVIDIA Quadro RTX 6000 GPUs, 24 GB each; about 24-30 h per optimization run, one prompt per victim agent), within reach of a typical team; it is an attack, not a development approach
fields.quote: Each model is deployed on up to two NVIDIA Quadro RTX 6000 GPUs (24 GB each), depending on its size. Under this setup, a full optimization run takes approximately 24 to 30 hours
fields.why: Q13 applies to studies that propose an approach; if PackHallu is taken as the proposed approach, its requirements are stated and modest, so N/A would not follow the rule.
fields.doubt: Só muda se aceitares 'Proposes an approach' na natureza. Nesse caso o Q13 aplica-se: a pág. 23 dá os requisitos (até duas GPUs de 24 GB, 24-30 h por otimização). Decide Sim ou Parcial; se mantiveres Evaluates, fica N/A.

fields.v: Partly (0.5): the authors created PackHallu and the Repeat Attack baseline, and co-authors also wrote the Combined Attack [11] (Gong) and ObliInjection [13] (R. Wang, Gong) baselines; GCG, TAP and all evaluated agent frameworks and LLMs are external
fields.quote: We compare PackHallu with five representative prompt injection attack baselines, comprising two heuristic-based attacks and three optimization-based attacks.
fields.where: §6.1 Experimental Setup, Compared attacks, p. 8; references [11], [13], p. 20
fields.why: The authors' own attack is compared with external ones (GCG, TAP) under the same setting, so the rule gives Partly, not No.
fields.doubt: O PackHallu é dos autores, mas é comparado com ataques externos (GCG e TAP, pág. 9). Pela regra, isso dá Parcial. Nota: o Combined Attack e o ObliInjection também são de coautores (refs. [11] e [13], pág. 20). Confirma e muda para Parcial (0.5).

fields.v: Attention proportion on malicious prompt; correlation of success with package popularity (PyPI downloads) and agent capability; trajectory categories in Claude Code case study; detector FNR and FPR; SASR (share of tasks where malicious package imported) and DASR (malicious package imported and code executes, malicious behaviour triggered); SASR computed on the tasks where the agent imports the victim package under benign conditions, DASR on those where it also imports it and the code executes under benign conditions.
fields.quote: and the generated code also executes successfully under benign conditions.
fields.where: §6.1 Evaluation metrics, SASR and DASR definitions, pp. 11-12
fields.why: The denominators are tasks where the agent correctly imports the victim package (SASR) or imports it and the code executes (DASR) under benign conditions, not tasks the agent solves correctly.
fields.doubt: O registo diz que SASR/DASR contam só tarefas 'resolvidas corretamente'. O artigo (págs. 11-12) usa tarefas em que o agente importa o pacote certo (SASR) e, para o DASR, em que também executa sem erro. Não exige solução correta. Confirma e ajusta a frase.
